facts.statement: Avolatavis fossils have been found in the early Eocene Green River Formation in Wyoming and the London Clay in Essex, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: known from the early Eocene Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation of Wyoming, United States, and from the London Clay of Walton-on-the-Naze (Essex, United Kingdom)

facts.statement: The genus Avolatavis was first described by Daniel T. Ksepka and Julia A. Clarke in 2012, with Avolatavis tenens as the type species.
facts.quote: It was first named by Daniel T. Ksepka and Julia A. Clarke in 2012 and the type species is Avolatavis tenens

facts.statement: A second species, Avolatavis europaeus, was described by Gerald Mayr and Andrew C. Kitchener in 2023.
facts.quote: Gerald Mayr and Andrew C. Kitchener described the second species, A. europaeus, in 2023

facts.statement: Avolatavis is classified as an extinct stem-parrot or a member of the stem group leading to parrots and passerines.
facts.quote: Avolatavis is an extinct genus of stem-parrot (pan-psittaciform) or a member of the stem group of Psittacopasseres

facts.statement: Researchers assigned Avolatavis to the family Vastanavidae, which may represent early diverging stem parrots or stem representatives of the parrot and passerine clade.
facts.quote: Mayr and Kitchener assigned Avolatavis to the family Vastanavidae, which might be early diverging stem group presentatives of Pan-Psittaciformes or stem group representatives of Psittacopasseres

facts.statement: Avolatavis is placed within the order Psittaciformes.
Avolatavis belongs to the class Aves.
Avolatavis is part of the infraclass Neognathae.
Avolatavis is an animal belonging to the kingdom Animalia.
Avolatavis is a member of the phylum Chordata.
Avolatavis is a vertebrate belonging to the subphylum Vertebrata.
